copy.blurb:
The model fancies Curaçao more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against Côte d'Ivoire. +7.9pp is a substantive gap; that's what fires this as a Pick on the home side.

On Elo, Côte d'Ivoire comes in 240 points ahead — Curaçao at 1480, Côte d'Ivoire at 1720. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Curaçao to win at 17%, the draw at 16%, and Côte d'Ivoire to win at 67%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. Curaçao on the win side reads 17%.

On the same three-way, Kalshi: Curaçao to win at 9%, the draw at 16%, and Côte d'Ivoire to win at 74%. Kalshi has Curaçao at 9%, which prices out at American odds of +1011; the model has the same side at 17%. The +7.9pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Curaçao, that haircut lands the model at 13%; the market is at 9%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +3.8pp. The point is selection, not a blanket call. Most matches the model and the market agree on. This is one of the ones where they don't, and the gap is on the Curaçao side specifically.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 34 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read.
drivers: Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
Bootstrap lower-bound on the Curaçao side still clears the Pick threshold.
Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
Pre-match Elo gives Curaçao a stronger prior than the Kalshi line implies.
copy.summary: The home side reads stronger to the model than to the market. Our Elo prior puts Curaçao at 17%; Kalshi prices that side at 9%. The +7.9pp gap calls a Pick.
copy.title: Curaçao v Côte d'Ivoire · the model leans Curaçao
